item.content:encoded:
The portion of SCP-511 that does not comprise SCP-511-1 consists of other biomass; small rodents, various plant materials, insects and insect larvae, black mold, a human [DATA EXPUNGED]

It goes from general enumeration, to so specific item.
"human remains" might work, or if the shock-value is needed, "in one instance a human [DATA EXPUNGED]"
The way it is right now seems to imply every instance has a specific human 'something', and that would be something to be described on it's own rather than buried along the generic non-cat matter.

item.title: How does someone submit an old SCP for editing?

item.content:encoded:
[Disclaimer: there is no canon, yada yada]

The Foundation wouldn't just burn it down, blow it up, or otherwise destroy 'extra' sites as long as two things are true:

1) They can be contained with a reasonable cost in life and resources,
2) The Foundation can learn something from those secondary sites.

These seem to be pretty reasonably contained under ordinary conditions, and there's definitely stuff to be learned by having more than one to study, so why try to destroy them all? Secure, Contain, Protect: lock it up, keep everyone safe from it, and keep it intact. It's not like the Foundation wasn't to destroy all this stuff—that's the GOC's job.

Well that last bit was to plug a bit of a plot hole; why the Foundation doesn't just nuke it from orbit. I believe these do just "happen," and the Foundation is dealing with a growing number of SCP-511 sites all the time, because it appears that destroying an SCP-511 might cause a containment breach.

Of course, the obvious theory is that one or more escaped SCP-511-1 from the breach were "carriers" and incorporated themselves into another site. (After ingesting some pieces of Foundation personnel during the attack.) But, given this thing doesn't follow rational biological rules, we just don't know…

I was thinking "Eh, OK, it's an undead hateful cat that makes other cats hate people" and wondering why this was strongly positive, when it seemed pretty blah, the kind of thing that gets a few upvotes, a few downvotes, and eventually drifts to negative five for a rewrite.

Then I read the agent's story, and it was all brought together. Normally I hate it when the addendums have to carry an article, but here it wouldn't work nearly as well if the reveal wasn't the very last thing I read. Outstanding work; this will earn its spot on the top rated SCPs.

The only aspect I disliked was the bit about killing it causing another to pop up. I think that these being naturally occurring, but always just a little different, would be a bit more unsettling than having to control a largely static number of sites.

item.content:encoded:
Alright. A post like this really ticks me off, and I'm having a bad day, so I'm going to tell you why.

It's dismissive. It's like you looked at it, saw the picture, downvoted, and came in here to make that comment. To paraphrase Ghost from the Rules of Thumb page, if all you can do is point to a list to say something is bad, then it's probably not that bad. In this case, it isn't bad at all. It's damn good. So please. Reread and, if it still sucks, leave your vote there. But do not downvote because you read something on a god damned list and didn't take the time to read the disclaimer.

Right. I feel better now.

That being said: Well done, sandewswann. I am going to keep my eye on you.
